pharm: Organochlorine (gamma isomer of hexachlorocyclohexane) absorbed through the chitinous exoskeleton of mites and lice, causing CNS stimulation, convulsions, and death of the parasite; the same mechanism produces neurotoxicity if systemically absorbed by humans.
quick: Scabies: 1% lotion thin layer neck-down, single application, wash off after 8-12 h. Lice: 1% shampoo to dry hair, lather, rinse after 4 minutes
Topical use; not related to meals
Category C; weigh risk-benefit, consider safer alternatives
Excreted in breast milk; interrupt nursing for at least 24 hours after use
No specific topical adjustment; minimize systemic exposure
Caution - severe hepatic impairment increases neurotoxicity risk
Watch for CNS effects (dizziness, tremor, seizures); skin irritation
summary: Lindane (gamma benzene hexachloride) is a topical organochlorine used to treat scabies (1% lotion) and head and pubic (crab) lice (1% shampoo). It carries a boxed warning for CNS neurotoxicity, including seizures and deaths, reported mainly with overuse but rarely even after a single correct application. It is therefore reserved as a second-line agent only for patients who cannot tolerate or have failed other approved therapies. Treatment is a single thin application: lotion is left on 8-12 hours then washed off; shampoo is left on dry hair for exactly 4 minutes then lathered and rinsed. It must not be retreated. It is contraindicated in premature neonates and uncontrolled seizure disorders, and used with extreme caution in patients under 50 kg (110 lb), infants, children, the elderly, and those with conditions that increase absorption.
indications: Treatment of scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei) - 1% lotion - in patients who cannot tolerate or have failed first-line therapy
Treatment of head lice (Pediculus capitis) and pubic/crab lice (Phthirus pubis) - 1% shampoo - second-line

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer over the entire skin from the neck down; about 1 ounce for an average adult, maximum 2 ounces for larger adults. Leave on 8-12 hours, then wash off completely. Single application only
dosage.n: Do not retreat; total body application from neck down only

dosage.d: Use the minimum amount needed to cover; use with extreme caution if under ~50 kg (110 lb)
dosage.n: Higher systemic absorption per body weight in children/infants

dosage.d: Apply about 1 ounce (up to 2 ounces for longer/denser hair) to DRY hair without water; work in and leave for exactly 4 minutes, then add water to lather and rinse thoroughly; comb out nits
dosage.n: Time the 4 minutes precisely; do not retreat or reuse

dosage.d: Do not exceed 2 ounces; do not repeat the application
dosage.n: Repeat or prolonged use markedly increases seizure/neurotoxicity risk

admin: Confirm the diagnosis before use and reserve for patients who have failed or cannot tolerate first-line agents
Lotion (scabies): apply a thin layer to clean, dry, cool skin from the neck down only; do not apply to face. Wash off after 8-12 hours
Shampoo (lice): apply to dry hair without adding water, leave on exactly 4 minutes, then lather with a little water and rinse fully; remove nits with a fine-tooth comb
Do not apply to open wounds, raw, inflamed, or irritated skin, or to skin conditions that increase absorption (e.g., crusted scabies, atopic dermatitis, psoriasis)
Use a single application only - do NOT retreat even if living mites/itch persist (itch can last weeks)
Wash bedding and clothing in hot water; treat close/sexual contacts as appropriate
Apply only the directed amount; do not exceed 2 ounces
moa: Lindane is absorbed through the chitinous exoskeleton (and respiratory system) of mites and lice. As an organochlorine, it acts on the parasite nervous system - antagonizing GABA-gated chloride channels and producing neuronal hyperexcitation, convulsions, and death of the parasite and its ova. The same neuroexcitatory mechanism is responsible for lindane's central nervous system toxicity in humans when it is absorbed systemically, which is greatest in small/low-weight patients and when too much is applied or it is left on too long.

absolute: Premature (preterm) neonates - immature, more permeable skin and immature metabolism
Known hypersensitivity to lindane or any component
Application to acutely inflamed or raw skin, crusted (Norwegian) scabies, atopic dermatitis, or psoriasis (markedly increased absorption)
relative: Patients weighing less than approximately 50 kg (110 lb), including infants and children
Conditions that increase the risk of seizures or absorption (HIV infection, history of head trauma, severe hepatic cirrhosis, medications that lower the seizure threshold)
monitor: Neurologic symptoms (dizziness, restlessness, tremor, seizures) after application

preg: Pregnancy Category C. Lindane crosses the placenta and is systemically absorbed; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus, and consider safer alternatives first given the neurotoxicity profile.
lact: Lindane is excreted in human breast milk. If treatment is necessary in a nursing mother, breastfeeding should be interrupted for at least 24 hours after application to limit infant exposure.
renal: No specific topical dosage adjustment is defined. Because the concern is systemic neurotoxicity from absorbed drug, minimize the amount applied and contact time, especially in any patient with impaired clearance.
hepatic: Lindane is metabolized hepatically; severe hepatic impairment (e.g., cirrhosis) may reduce clearance and increase the risk of CNS toxicity. Use with extreme caution.

major: Drugs that lower the seizure threshold (e.g., certain antipsychotics, antidepressants, tramadol, systemic antimalarials, theophylline) - increased seizure risk with lindane absorption
moderate: Other topical agents, oils, or occlusive dressings applied to the same area - may increase lindane absorption
Concurrent neurotoxic agents - additive CNS toxicity
interactions.food: Not applicable - topical use, no meal relationship.
interactions.alcohol: No specific topical interaction identified, but avoid additional CNS depressants/stimulants that could compound neurotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: Systemic absorption can produce measurable blood lindane levels; correlates with neurotoxicity risk.

common: Itching or burning at application site
serious: CNS stimulation ranging from dizziness and restlessness to convulsions
Seizures (rare, even after correct single use)
emergency: Death (reported, especially with overuse or in vulnerable patients)

monitoring: Observe for CNS effects (dizziness, restlessness, tremor, seizures), especially in low-weight, pediatric, or elderly patients
Assess local skin tolerance and irritation
Confirm a single correct application and that the patient understands NOT to retreat
Re-evaluate treatment failure microscopically rather than reapplying
counsel: Use this medicine exactly once - do NOT reapply, even if itching continues (itching can last 2-4 weeks after the mites are gone)
Lotion: put a thin layer on dry skin from the neck down only, wash it off after 8 to 12 hours; do not put it on the face or on broken/irritated skin
Shampoo: put it on completely DRY hair, leave it on for exactly 4 minutes (use a clock), then add water, lather, and rinse well; comb out the nits
Do not use more than the amount your pharmacist or doctor told you (do not exceed 2 ounces)
Stop and get medical help right away if you feel dizzy, restless, have muscle twitching, or have a seizure
Keep away from the eyes, mouth, and out of reach of children; wash bedding and clothing in hot water
pk: Parasiticidal on contact; kills mites/lice during the single application period
Peak blood level about 64 ng/mL roughly 6 hours after lotion application
pearls: Boxed warning: CNS neurotoxicity, seizures, and deaths - reserve as SECOND-LINE only after other agents fail or cannot be tolerated
Single thin application only; never retreat - most toxicity follows repeat/prolonged use or excess amount
Contraindicated in premature neonates and uncontrolled seizure disorders
Use with extreme caution if under ~50 kg (110 lb): infants, children, and the elderly are most vulnerable
Lotion = scabies (8-12 h, neck down); shampoo = lice (exactly 4 minutes on dry hair); do not interchange
Persistent itch after treatment is not treatment failure - do not reapply; evaluate before any repeat course
missed: This medicine is given as a single application, so there is no regular dosing schedule and no dose to make up. Do not apply an extra dose; if you believe treatment failed, contact your clinician rather than reapplying.
overdose: Accidental ingestion or excessive topical absorption can cause CNS toxicity - nausea, vomiting, restlessness, tremor, and seizures, which may progress to respiratory failure and death. There is no specific antidote. Remove the product (wash skin), provide supportive care, control seizures with benzodiazepines/anticonvulsants, and protect the airway; avoid oil-based laxatives after ingestion as they increase absorption. Seek emergency/poison-control care immediately.
